question: In community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) managed in an outpatient setting with CURB-65 score of 0–1, oral amoxicillin monotherapy (without adding a macrolide) is an appropriate first-line empirical regimen for a patient with no atypical features.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is actually true. Amoxicillin monotherapy is appropriate for low-severity CAP (CURB-65 0–1) in otherwise healthy outpatients; combination with a macrolide is reserved for patients with features suggesting atypical pathogens or for moderate-severity CAP requiring hospitalisation.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. For low-severity outpatient CAP (CURB-65 0–1) without features suggesting atypical pathogens, oral amoxicillin 500 mg three times daily is a guideline-concordant first choice; a macrolide is added only when atypical cover is specifically needed.
